title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 382 (Display of name, etc., of foreign company)

content.overview: Every foreign company shall conspicuously exhibit on the outside of every office or place where it carries on business in India the name of the company and the country in which it is incorporated, in letters easily legible in English characters and also in the characters of the language or one of the languages in general use in the locality. It shall also cause the name of the company and of the country in which the company is incorporated to be stated in legible English characters in all business letters, bill-heads and letter paper, and in all notices and other official publications of the company. Where the liability of the members of the company is limited, the company shall cause notice of that fact to be stated in every such prospectus, notice, circular, advertisement and official publication and in all business letters, bill-heads, letter paper and in all other official publications in legible characters.
content.glance: Display company name and country of incorporation outside every Indian place of business and on business stationery; if limited liability, state that fact on publications and stationery.
content.study: Section 382 requires foreign companies to display their name and country of incorporation outside every Indian place of business (in English and a local language) and on business letters, bill-heads, letter paper, notices and official publications. Where members’ liability is limited, that fact must also be stated on the specified documents. The purpose is to put persons dealing with the company on notice of its identity, origin and limited-liability status.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.body: A foreign company must display its name and country of incorporation outside every Indian place of business and on business stationery; if limited liability, that fact must also be stated.

provisions.title: Display of name, etc., of foreign company

examples.title: Illustration — s. 382
examples.body: A German limited company with an office in Bengaluru exhibits its name and ‘Germany’ outside the office in English and Kannada, and states limited liability on its letterheads under s. 382.

hypotheticals.question: What is the core effect of s. 382?
hypotheticals.analysis: It requires foreign companies to display name, country of incorporation and (where applicable) limited-liability status at Indian places of business and on stationery.

rows.left: Display of name of foreign company
rows.right: Accounts (s. 381) or service on foreign company (s. 383)

misconceptions.trap: Assuming English-only display is always sufficient.
misconceptions.correction: s. 382 also requires display in the characters of a language in general use in the locality.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should s. 382 be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm foreign-company status and Indian place of business. II. Check name, country and limited-liability display on premises and stationery. III. Conclude.
